_doc: PLAYCRAFT genre intelligence. A game gets every genre whose score is close enough to the best (multi-label). Each profile: doc_keywords (README/docs, strongest evidence), code_keywords (source), weights (category multipliers for the overall score), priorities (what matters most in this genre), questions (genre-specific prompts per discipline), criteria (genre checks: `signals` are core signal ids, `patterns` are extra source regexes; any match = present), testing (how to test this genre), avoid (systems that do not belong). Recommendations here override the generic ones for this genre.

physics_puzzle.title: Physics puzzle / destruction
priorities: skill shots that read as skill
impact feedback scaled to the size of the event

design_architect: Is there a clear target and a readable way to cause the outcome, or does the player just spam until things fall?
Do multiple solutions exist, and does the game recognise the clever one?
game_feel: Does a big collapse feel bigger than a small knock (shake, slow-mo and sound scaled by mass/impulse)?
Does the aim/release feel intentional (anticipation, release snap, a beat before impact)?
loop_designer: How long between a shot and the next decision? Is the player watching settling debris for too long?
difficulty_balance: Can every level be solved with the real controls (automated solver/par runs)?

criteria.title: Fixed-step, deterministic physics
criteria.recommendation: Step the physics at a fixed rate (e.g. 60/120 Hz with an accumulator) and seed every random source, so the same shot always gives the same outcome; players can only learn a system that is consistent.

criteria.title: Emergent chain reactions
criteria.recommendation: Let falling pieces transfer damage (impulse above a threshold breaks what they land on) and celebrate the chain with a counter; chains turn one good shot into a story.

criteria.title: Destruction reads physically (debris, dust, pieces)
criteria.recommendation: Break objects into a few pieces with debris and dust on impact rather than deleting them; scale particles by impulse, not per hit.

criteria.title: Skill shots are recognised
criteria.recommendation: Name the skill when it happens (BANK SHOT, CHAIN x5) with a short, readable callout; recognition is what turns physics accidents into mastery.

criteria.title: Aim preview / trajectory guide
criteria.recommendation: Show a short trajectory preview (to the first contact, not the full path) so aiming is a decision, not a guess.

criteria.title: Levels proven solvable (solver / par tests)
criteria.recommendation: Add a headless test that finishes every level with the real controls (a scripted or searched solution) and records par; it catches impossible levels and exploits before players do.

testing: Determinism: replay the same input twice and compare the settled state
Solver: finish each level headlessly with the real controls; record par
Impact feedback: shake/particles scale with impulse (small knock < collapse)
Settle time: seconds from shot to next decision
avoid: shot timers that rush a thinking game
random damage rolls that break consistency

arcade.title: Arcade
priorities: a difficulty ramp you can feel

loop_designer: How many seconds from death to playing again?
What changes between minute 1 and minute 3 of a run?
game_feel: Does a near-miss feel like a near-miss (slow-mo, sound, callout)?
Is every point scored visible where the eye already is?
retention_replay: Is the best score always in view? Is there a reason to beat it (unlock, rank, grade)?

criteria.title: Instant restart after failure
criteria.recommendation: Restart on the same button that plays, within a second of the crash animation; no menus between runs.

criteria.title: Near-miss / close-call feedback
criteria.recommendation: Detect near misses and reward them (a beat of slow-mo, a sound, a small bonus); it turns danger into excitement.

criteria.title: Persistent best score
criteria.recommendation: Save the best score and show it on the start and game-over screens with the gap to beat.

criteria.title: Difficulty ramps within a run
criteria.recommendation: Ramp speed/spawn density with distance or time on a curve that plateaus; the player should feel minute 2 is harder than minute 1.

criteria.title: Score changes are celebrated where the player looks
criteria.recommendation: Pop the points at the place they were earned and pulse the score counter; feedback must arrive where the eye already is.

testing: Time from game over to the next run (target < 2 s)
Run length distribution of a bot with simple inputs
Score/spawn curves over time from exposed state
Input → response under 100 ms
avoid: currencies and upgrade trees that make the core skill irrelevant

platformer.title: Platformer

controls_device: Can the player jump a few frames after leaving a ledge and a few frames before landing?
Does releasing jump early cut the jump?
game_feel: Is there squash on landing and a dust puff, and does the character turn around without sliding?

criteria.title: Coyote time and jump buffering
criteria.recommendation: Accept a jump ~80-120 ms after leaving a ledge (coyote time) and remember a jump pressed ~100 ms before landing (buffer). Players blame themselves less and the controls feel 'tight'.

criteria.title: Variable jump height
criteria.recommendation: Cut upward velocity when jump is released early so short taps make short hops.

criteria.title: Acceleration and friction curves
criteria.recommendation: Use separate ground/air acceleration and friction instead of instant velocity; tune turnaround to be faster than start-up.

criteria.title: Checkpoints and fast respawn
criteria.recommendation: Respawn at the last checkpoint in under a second.

testing: Scripted jump timing tests (coyote/buffer windows) against exposed state
Max jump distance vs level gaps (every gap is clearable)
Respawn time after a death

survival.title: Survival
priorities: survival tension from real resource pressure

design_architect: What does the player have to give up to get what they need? If nothing, there is no tension.
Does the world tell its story through places and finds?
loop_designer: Is there a moment every few minutes where the player must decide to push further or turn back?
difficulty_balance: Can the player run out of the critical resource, and do they see it coming?
Is the early game too generous (no pressure) or too punishing (death before learning)?
player_experience: Can the player navigate by landmarks and the map, or only by following a marker?

criteria.title: Resource pressure exists
criteria.recommendation: Make one resource the clock (fuel, oxygen, hull) and make the player choose between spending it and exploring further.

criteria.title: Failure is telegraphed (low-resource warnings)
criteria.recommendation: Warn before failure: a gauge colour change at 25%, a sound at 10%, a clear 'turn back' moment.

criteria.title: Exploration pays off (discoveries, finds, catalogue)
criteria.recommendation: Put something worth finding behind every detour (a story find, a rare resource, a shortcut) and log it in a catalogue.

criteria.title: Navigation aids (map, compass, landmarks)
criteria.recommendation: Give a map and a compass but make landmarks visible from afar; navigation should be a skill, not a marker-follow.

criteria.title: Day/night or weather that changes play
criteria.recommendation: Tie night/storms to real risk (visibility, damage, fuel burn) so atmosphere becomes tension.

criteria.title: Environmental storytelling
criteria.recommendation: Tell the world's story through places and finds (logs, wrecks, notes) rather than cutscenes.

testing: Resource curve: simulate a session and plot the critical resource (does it ever get tight?)
Time-to-first-death for a careless bot vs a careful one
Every critical warning appears before the failure
avoid: timers that punish exploration without warning

simulation.title: Simulation
priorities: systems the player can read (gauges, feedback)
a reason to master the simulation

design_architect: Which part of the simulation does the player act on, and can they see it respond?
controls_device: Do vehicles feel different from each other and from walking?

criteria.title: Systems are readable (gauges, indicators)
criteria.recommendation: Surface the simulated state the player acts on (gauges, forecasts, scanner readouts) in one glance.

criteria.title: Time controls (skip, sleep, speed)
criteria.recommendation: Let the player skip dead time (sleep, fast-forward, travel) so the simulation never becomes waiting.

criteria.title: Simulation rules covered by tests
criteria.recommendation: Unit-test the rules (handling limits, weather effects) so tuning changes do not silently break play.

testing: Handling envelope tests (top speed, climb angle) from the sim directly
Time-skip and save/restore round trips

strategy.title: Strategy

design_architect: Is there a dominant strategy? Do two good players play differently?
player_experience: Can the player predict the result of an action before committing (damage preview, range)?

criteria.title: Outcome previews and tooltips
criteria.recommendation: Preview the outcome of every action before it is committed (damage, range, cost).

criteria.title: Undo / confirm for irreversible actions
criteria.recommendation: Allow undo of the last move (or confirm irreversible ones) so mistakes are about strategy, not input.

criteria.title: Opponent AI
criteria.recommendation: Give the AI a readable plan and difficulty levels; test it against scripted strategies.

testing: AI vs AI matches across seeds (win rates per strategy)
Exploit search for dominant openings
avoid: real-time pressure on a thinking game without a pause

roguelike.title: Roguelike / roguelite
priorities: meta progression that widens options rather than inflating stats

loop_designer: Do two runs feel different by minute 5?
progression: Does meta progression add options or just numbers?

criteria.title: Seeded runs
criteria.recommendation: Seed the generator per run and show the seed so good runs can be shared and bugs reproduced.

criteria.title: Run variety (procedural content, build choices)
criteria.recommendation: Vary layouts and offer build-defining picks every few minutes.

criteria.title: Meta progression between runs
criteria.recommendation: Unlock new options (characters, items) between runs rather than permanent stat inflation.

testing: Generate 100 seeds: every layout is completable
Run-length and win-rate distribution per build
avoid: runs longer than the session the platform allows

incremental.title: Incremental / idle

progression: How long between new unlocks at hour 1 and hour 5?
Does prestige change strategy or only multiply?

criteria.title: Offline progress
criteria.recommendation: Compute progress while away (capped) and show a welcome-back summary.

criteria.title: Large-number formatting
criteria.recommendation: Format large numbers with suffixes (1.2K, 3.4M) consistently.

criteria.title: Prestige / reset layer
criteria.recommendation: Add a reset layer that grants a new mechanic, not just a multiplier.

testing: Simulate 10 h of optimal play: time between unlocks never exceeds the target

racing.title: Racing

game_feel: Does speed feel fast (FOV, camera, particles, sound pitch)?
difficulty_balance: Does the AI rubber-band so hard that the player's lead is meaningless?

criteria.title: Sense of speed (FOV, speed lines, camera)
criteria.recommendation: Widen FOV and pull the camera back slightly with speed; add speed lines and pitch the engine sound with RPM.

criteria.title: Time trial / ghost
criteria.recommendation: Record the best lap as a ghost and show splits at checkpoints.

criteria.title: Checkpoints / lap structure
criteria.recommendation: Make checkpoints and the next gate always readable; reset to the track quickly.

testing: AI lap-time spread vs player bot
Track completion by an autopilot on every course
avoid: upgrade grinds that replace driving skill

exploration.title: Exploration / adventure
priorities: traversal that feels good on its own
discoveries that are logged and rewarded

loop_designer: What makes the player turn off the road? Can they see something interesting from where they stand?
presentation: Does the world move and react (wind, wildlife, weather) when the player stands still?

criteria.title: Discoveries are logged (catalogue, journal, map)
criteria.recommendation: Log every discovery somewhere the player revisits (catalogue, board, map) with a count of what's left.

criteria.title: Secrets and hidden things
criteria.recommendation: Hide a few things off the main paths and hint at them (a glint, a sound, a companion reacting).

criteria.title: Map / orientation
criteria.recommendation: A map that marks discoveries and the player, opened from one button.

testing: Traversal: time to cross the world by each means
Every discovery reachable (scripted route or nav check)

sandbox.title: Sandbox

design_architect: What can the player make or cause that the designer did not script?

criteria.title: Sandbox / free-play mode
criteria.recommendation: Offer a goal-free mode with every tool unlocked.

criteria.title: Save and share creations
criteria.recommendation: Let players save, name and share a creation (a code or a link).

testing: Stress: spawn many objects and measure frame time
Save/load round-trip of a creation

action.title: Action

game_feel: When a hit lands, does time stop for a few frames and does the target react?
difficulty_balance: Can the player see every attack coming?

criteria.title: Hit feedback (hit-stop, flash, knockback)
criteria.recommendation: On a landed hit: 40-80 ms hit-stop, a white flash on the target, knockback along the hit direction, a punchy sound. Scale by damage.

criteria.title: Enemy attacks are telegraphed
criteria.recommendation: Give every enemy attack a wind-up pose/flash proportional to its damage.

criteria.title: Invulnerability frames / dodge
criteria.recommendation: Brief invulnerability after taking damage and on dodge prevents unfair multi-hits.

testing: Damage taken per minute by a bot; hit feedback events per hit
Every attack has a telegraph ≥ 300 ms

sports.title: Sports

controls_device: Is the skill in the input (timing, power) visible and learnable?

criteria.title: Timing / power input with feedback
criteria.recommendation: Show the timing/power window and rate each attempt (perfect/good/early/late).

criteria.title: Contact moment feels impactful
criteria.recommendation: Freeze 2-3 frames on contact, a crisp sound and a camera punch on great contact.

testing: Input window tests: the perfect window exists and is reachable
Result distribution for a bot at different skill levels
avoid: stat upgrades that replace timing skill

management_builder.title: Management / builder
priorities: economy feedback (where does money come from and go)

progression: Does the base visibly grow as the player progresses?
player_experience: Can the player see income/expenses and the effect of a build before placing it?

criteria.title: Placement preview / snapping
criteria.recommendation: Show a ghost of the piece with valid/invalid colouring and snap to the grid before placing.

criteria.title: Economy feedback
criteria.recommendation: Show cost before buying and a running income/expense summary.

criteria.title: Structural stability feedback
criteria.recommendation: Colour or creak stressed parts before they fail so collapses feel caused, not random.

testing: Economy simulation: funds over a long session never stall or explode
Undo/demolish round-trips
avoid: build timers that just make the player wait

hybrid_experimental.title: Hybrid / experimental
priorities: a clear identity: what is the one thing only this game does
each borrowed genre's core done well enough

design_architect: Can the pitch be said in one sentence? Which genre's expectations does the player bring, and does the game meet or deliberately subvert them?

criteria.title: Unfamiliar mechanics are taught by doing
criteria.recommendation: Teach each unfamiliar mechanic in a safe first encounter (show, then let them try) instead of a text wall.

testing: First-session test: can a bot following on-screen prompts reach the first goal?
avoid: forcing the game into one genre's checklist
